title: Grok out of credits on stderr is classified, so the role falls back
lead: When grok prints its credits or spending-limit error outside a stream event (on stderr or as a plain `Error:` line on stdout), the round's exit is out_of_credits with the same fixed reason as today, so the role falls back to the next matrix row and grok is marked out.
findings_note: 2026-11-18 03:38 UTC: S388 (run ork-20261117-233556-f24d) implementer round 4 and gate round 5 ran grok-4.7 and each ended in under a second with exit "unclassified", no report, and the run stopped. A manual `grok -p "reply with ok"` (grok 1.0.77) printed `Error: Internal error: { "message": "API error (status 403 Forbidden): Your team <team> has either used all available credits or reached its monthly spending limit. ...", "http_status": 403 }` on its output and exited 0. The adapter looks for `used all available credits` only in stream `error` events (`internal/agent/grok/grok.go:291-309`) and sets out of credits only from that (`:380-381`), so the stderr form stays unclassified and the role neither falls back nor marks grok out.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Two S388 rounds stopped the run on 2026-11-18 because grok's credit error went unclassified; the orchestrator had to probe grok by hand and mark it out. Classifying vendor failures is deterministic work, and owner rule (2026-11-17) says such steps are code.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestGrokCreditsOnStderrIsOutOfCredits` in `internal/agent/grok/grok_test.go`: a fake grok that prints the 403 `Error: Internal error: {...used all available credits...}` text on stderr, no stream events, exit 0; the round's exit is out_of_credits and the reason is the fixed text that does not name the team.
- `TestGrokCreditsOnStdoutPlainLineIsOutOfCredits`: the same text as a plain non-JSON stdout line; out_of_credits.
- `TestGrokBadModelAndAuthStayUnclassified` still passes.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests and see them red for the stated reason.
2. After the process exits, if no stream event set credits, check stderr and any non-JSON stdout lines for `creditsText` and `usageLimitText` and set the same exits and fixed reasons as `fail` does.
3. Never copy the vendor message (it names the team) into the reason or a report.
4. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet at the end of `## Unreleased`, written by hand.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- A grok round whose credits or spending-limit error appears only on stderr or a plain stdout line ends out_of_credits, and the role falls back to the next row.
- The reason does not contain the team id.
- Other unclassified exits stay unclassified.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/agent/grok -run 'TestGrokCreditsOnStderrIsOutOfCredits|TestGrokCreditsOnStdoutPlainLineIsOutOfCredits|TestGrokBadModelAndAuthStayUnclassified' -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` must print nothing.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, message "Grok credits error on stderr is out of credits".
